title: Prepare a wet microscope mount without large air bubbles
instruction: Prepare a wet microscope mount of the printed letter using one drop of distilled water. Leave the coverslip centered over the letter with no large air bubbles.
context: Common wet-mount preparation requires advancing the water front under a held glass coverslip without sealing in an air pocket. The robot doses a slide bearing an inert printed letter and seats the separate coverslip. [Wet-mount protocol](https://openwa.pressbooks.pub/lwtechbiol160/chapter/lab-1-care-and-use-of-compound-microscopes/)
setup: On a 104 × 61 mm dark inspection cradle, a loose 75 × 25 × 1 mm clear glass slide lies 385 mm forward and 12 mm left of the arm midpoint, with a 6 mm printed letter at its center. A loose 22 × 22 × 0.22 mm glass coverslip rests on two supports 374 mm forward and 105 mm right. An upright single-dose rubber-bulb dropper holds 25 µL of distilled water 347 mm forward and 147 mm left. Fixed pad and tool rest heights, materials and ready pose are in the README.
scoring: 0 for no valid drop. 0.25 for a drop within 10 mm along and 7 mm across from the letter. 0.55 when a centered flat coverslip also has more than 60% wet coverage. 0.80 for at least 82% wet coverage and no air pocket above 2 mm in diameter. 1.0 when that result remains stable on the pad for 0.5 seconds with both grippers at least 39 mm away. The coverslip center must be within 3 mm along and 2.5 mm across from the letter; all four corners must be within 1 mm of the slide plane. Use a macro photograph, grid and ruler. Either arm may perform either action.
reset_notes: Dry the slide, pad and slip, check the slip for chips, refill the single-dose dropper, place the three loose items at the listed positions and home both YAM arms with open jaws.
fidelity: Native contacts handle the loose slide, coverslip and spring bulb. Measured bulb and nozzle motion drive a one-drop supply. A geometric cap model uses measured coverslip approach and clearance to estimate wetting and air entrapment. Equal and opposite thin-film shear loads resist sliding after wet contact. Contrast tint makes the result visible. The model omits detailed surface tension, glass fracture and dissolved air.
scores: Demo: 1.0 in 420 actions. Dream-1: 0.0 after 590 actions.
